Box3D desktop compatibility

On this page ↓
Tested and untested configurationsExact build identityCompatibility layersEvidence and performance boundariesLater Web showcase evidence (2026-11-03)

Evidence snapshot: 2026-11-02. This describes the shared backend and distinct Kit and Replay adapters. The initial target pair remains macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64; a configured CI job is not an executed platform qualification.

Tested and untested configurations#

Configuration Kit Replay Actual scope and limits
macOS arm64 SDK/Native, official universal Godot launcher Exported pair PASS Exported pair PASS Native ARM64 processes on macOS15.8; target120, complete five-part bytes/signature, nonzero remote inputs, final ACK, natural exits and observed cleanup/one Native image. No Intel/universal SDK claim.
Linux x86_64 userspace/export, Rosetta in Linux aarch64 VM Exported pair PASS Exported pair PASS Actual ELF x86_64 Host/Client execution, translated functional evidence. Native Debug/Release twelve registered commands each were invoked by the direct runner; recorded CTest-run verdict is false, not rewritten to PASS.
Native Linux x86_64 hardware CI Not executed in these records Not executed in these records Intended CI target. Workflow/plan/source checks do not certify a remote job, throughput or hardware behavior.
macOS Intel / universal SDK Unqualified Unqualified Launcher contains an x86_64 slice, but supplied Core/scripts/modules/Native and selected execution are ARM64.
Windows Unqualified Box3D runtime Unqualified Box3D runtime Generic SDK cross-build evidence is separate; no current Box3D exported pair.
Web/mobile Unqualified Box3D runtime Unqualified Box3D runtime Generic browser SDK evidence does not qualify this Native shared-domain profile. No mobile/export claim.

The authoritative Gate C report (066df8b4a4ecbd8d97d505f06d3eeed6ebe044d5207b144016ba0a6a1dbac9ca) binds all four export/runtime records, raw PIDs, artifact hashes and source fences. Each pair reached120; all five parts matched within that pair. Each role observed one Native image and Native/wrapper/Meter cleanup0, with sample-owned owner delta0 against its actual baseline4. This is neither cross-platform state equality nor a new long-soak, frame-time or manual pixel/usability certification.

The later production suite adds current Kit and Replay exported108600-tick pairs on both configurations, each with more than1809 seconds after both GO observations, complete five-part equality, terminal ACKs, natural exits and observed cleanup. All eight300/3000ms service-pause cases passed. These headless authored scenes contain four bodies/four assets/one hinge; the separate Native stress bounds are unchanged. Sampled process RSS peaks were below129MB on macOS and186MB on translated Linux. RSS is separate from the 64MiB tracked physics admission limit and is not a general process-memory bound. See production-validation.md for allocation-lifetime regressions, the preserved earlier OOM/audit failures, CPU scope and exact records.

Deployment floor: the launcher plist declares11.0, but that is not the bundle requirement. The actual Kit export inspection inspect-rpaths-1..5.log under the report's p5-gate-c-kit-macos-export-v4 record shows SDK14.4/minos14.0 for the SDK/Native consumers; launcher log0 shows minos11.0. The Native manifest also records -mmacosx-version-min=14.0. Treat this bundle as requiring at least macOS14.0; actual execution was on15.8. macOS11..13 are not supported by this bundle, and a claimed minimum is not a substitute for an execution test.

Linux used Debian amd64 userspace in the recorded Podman/Rosetta environment. The VM6144MiB/container4096MiB/export compiler thread-count1 are build-resource settings, not a change to the simulation's64MiB admission cap. The Gate C report records the environment change and its rollback separately from product limits.

Exact build identity#

Both builds use float32, meters/Y-up/right-handed coordinates, fixed60Hz/four substeps and one simulation worker. Assertions and BOX3D_VALIDATE remain on in Debug and Release (-UNDEBUG overrides Release's -DNDEBUG). Effective engine/shim flags include -fno-fast-math -ffp-contract=off; no reassociation or FP-policy relaxation is implied by optimized export. Native observation is OFF.

The Gate C report's Native and export links contain exact compiler argv, resolved macros, manifests and deployed file hashes. macOS ad-hoc signing may change the deployment copy's file SHA; record source-to-deployed mapping and domain identity, not an assumed identical file hash. The common manifest version vector is recorded literally as [1,1,3,2,1]; catalog-selected recovery formats below are a separate contract. Build/target identities differ intentionally across targets.

The current production runs reused the later verified archive-cache build on macOS: source library SHA ed2c5fcfa8e0cbba5ee835c8cd9c73c35b6c3e03b4ac4ae1628a1fb946559371. The actual signed bundle copies are e3264dad2b9d60013bdd5a36e9385b2d62082a74886520e9dfd8e8ce61a8ff1a (Kit) and df3ddf2629d75cd6b0bf7eed6eb49e5a6eded4796c522644b03039cb201ca0a2 (Replay). Their recorded domain build/target remain the macOS identities above. Linux reused the recorded edfe2fd8… Release library and its original direct-command test manifest. The older Gate C file hashes remain historical inputs, not rewritten to the newer deployment bytes.

Keep35 bodies/shapes,32 initial dynamics, one joint, eight Native geometry assets, H128/prediction8/ordinary repair8 and64MiB tracked Native+snapshot+Host/reservations. RSS, rendering/engine overhead and build VM RAM are separate. Historical100/500 body probes did not expand this admitted profile. A scalar/SIMD/compiler/precision change requires a new identity and its own evidence.

Compatibility layers#

Layer Current declared contract
Opaque local solver image Resource2 / normalized solver dump3. Retained geometry/owners and exact compatible build/target/private ABI are required; bytes alone are not a portable saved state.
Native canonical recovery Primitive catalog format1; authored geometry format2; motion catalog format3. Trusted assets, semantic validation, scratch reconstruction and full reencode/compare remain mandatory.
Authoring Schema1 body/shape/resource identity retained; schema2 adds joint/character definitions. Current parsers explicitly accept the supported versions; no native handle is durable authoring data.
Owning bake artifact/import OGB3ART1, artifact/import version1,200-byte little-endian header, bounded definition bytes and checked source/shared-bake/content/integrity identity. Load rebakes once and validates before publication.
Motion/query API Version1, independent C/Odin layout queries for all13 records; this is not a recovery or network wire version.
Kit network World protocol2, current catalog/schema identity and signature/accepted-input confirmation. Native/authoring versions do not silently select another wire.
Replay network/archive Documented base protocol7/archive4 plus complete-physics codec/catalog/game/input contract fingerprints. Keep the actual READY/config/identity records; do not equate this with Kit World2 or Native recovery3.
Debug/presentation JSON Version1 with exact16hex epoch/tick/revision and explicit source; visualization is detached value data, outside canonical Game/Side.

Canonical encoding does not waive Native identity checks or establish mixed-target network compatibility. Current exports compare Host/Client on the same target; macOS-to-Linux exact solver agreement remains unclaimed. Unsupported versions, assets, references or identities must reject before replacing published state.

Evidence and performance boundaries#

  • Gate B, bounded macOS32-dynamic reference: original whole-call4ms requirement met by its declared final artifact streams. Older Dense sample9=8.894ms remains FAIL/causeUNKNOWN. Fact-burst CPU, Common normal and later Native feature builds are not inferred from that corpus.
  • Authoring, motion, editor and authored samples retain their exact earlier macOS scopes. Gate C adds the four normal exported pair results; it does not retroactively rerun those suites.
  • Remote hardware CI and future release qualification need actual job/run records. The desktop CLI's default is an inspectable plan, not a runtime PASS. See upgrade.md for the required maintainer gates and release changes.

Later Web showcase evidence (2026-11-03)#

The tables above retain their earlier desktop build scope. The later Dockyard handoff records an executed wasm32 backend and actual Chrome/Firefox multiplayer through the same reusable integration, plus a relocated macOS ARM64 SDK pair. Its current candidate is functionally passing but remains unqualified under the original Firefox correction maximum. This does not admit mobile or rewrite the earlier desktop hashes/failures. See the current build status.

A later bounded telemetry experiment on Firefox 159.0.1 retained every operation row until checked close. Its 610-second pair completed seven jobs with matching complete state and clean Native/Web ownership, but the Firefox normal maximum reached 29.56 ms against the unchanged 10 ms limit. Deferring telemetry did not resolve the rare stalls; their cause remains unknown. The attempted encoding reuse was restored after it showed no measured latency gain. These are separate experimental artifacts, and the earlier review archive remains unreleased and byte-identical.

A separate allocation-free signature reuse experiment copies a checksum-validated signature from an already-due, locally owned Snapshot, with exact tick, codec, epoch and peer scope checks. It preserves fact-before-chunk delivery and uses fresh encoding when reuse is unavailable. Native tests reduced solver-part materializations from two to one per recipient and preserved normative full5 bytes, receiver confirmation, failure recovery and balanced resources.

Its declared short Firefox 159.0.1 authority / Chrome 156.0.8078.80 comparison still rejected the strict maximum: baseline 30.600 ms, candidate 18.299 ms. Host p95 was 3.799 ms versus 3.800 ms, so no latency gain is established. Both pairs confirmed all five state parts and cleaned up; neither 60-second case establishes sustained admission. The unchanged sustained gate was not rerun. See the signature reuse report.

The optional transaction phase observations retain complete call timing and add bounded open/model/capture totals using the existing clock. Native and native-free Wasm tests cover nil/backward clocks, failed capture and unchanged state/cleanup. Captured slow calls distribute differently across the observed envelopes; the cause of the rare wall-time stalls remains unresolved. No clock overhead or outlier was subtracted.

A later frame egress change keeps complete-physics authority reception and publication inside the same public Room call, preparing its Snapshot after the current step. An actual browser counter run reduced old-head preparations from 486 to zero; native tests retain normative complete-wire bytes, receiver confirmation, zero-step publication, permission checks and balanced resources. Both final 610-second browser roles meet the original normal-frame limits. Firefox authority passes all measured budgets; Firefox client retains one 45.92 ms actual eight-step correction against the original 25 ms maximum (3,968 samples; p95=8.599 ms, p99=9.640 ms). That role is rejected. No outlier was removed and no unchanged sustained retry was run.

The audio lifetime fix stops and clears voices, then observes weak playback references until the mixer has released them before graceful quit or scene reload. Controlled active-sound exit, four simultaneous voices, muted exit and real leave/rejoin/rehost checks retain their own evidence. The original leaked AudioStreamPlaybackWAV resources and prior strict latency failures remain recorded. Public Internet validation, two-person feedback and the failed correction limit remain separate gates.
